newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria says democratic process no hurdle with EU.
newsitem.headline: Algeria says democratic process no hurdle with EU.

text.p: There is no link between the state of Algeria's democratic process and plans for an association accord with the European Union, Algeria's foreign affairs minister Ahmed Attaf said on Thursday.

Speaking after meeting European Parliament President Jose Maria Gil-Robles and the European Commissioner for EU relations with the Mediterranean Manuel Marin he said both issues had been discussed but Algeria's democratic process was "no obstacle" to a deal.
"There is no link between the democratic process in Algeria and the partnership process underway with the European Union," he told a news conference.
"We are carrying out this process at our own pace in line with what the Algerian people want, under a consensus with all the Algerian political class," he said.

Algeria has been without a parliament since 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a commanding lead. Violence erupted shortly after and about 60,000 people have died in the conflict.
Only on Thursday Algerian newspapers said Algeria's security forces had killed 40 Moslem guerillas including 12 shot during a gun battle of 12 hours.
Attaf said his country had "no complex" about human rights and that a discussion on this theme should "obviously include the situation of Algerian communities living abroad."
He said the association accord, on which negotiations started on March 4, should lead to an increase in investment in the country.
"The objective of this accord is the setting up of a free trade zone," he told a news conference.
"As a counterpart we expect Europe to take part in the rehabilitation of our industrial structure," he said, pointing to a negative growth in the sector.

The Algerian government will in April begin a series of meetings with the European Commission aimed at sealing a deal covering political dialogue, financial and economic cooperation and human and social relations.
